extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, third‑party requesters, and patent practitioners involved in inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules from the MPEP governing amendments, drawings, inventorship, fees, third‑party comments, service, timeliness, and examiner handling in inter partes reexamination proceedings. Covers what must be filed, how it must be presented, deadlines, permissible content, and consequences for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments which comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j) and 37 CFR 1.943 (and are formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b), and contain fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c)) will be entered in the reexamination file pursuant to the guidelines set forth in MPEP § 2234.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be formally presented and include required fees; see MPEP §2234 for entry guidelines. Form paragraphs (e.g., 22.12) may be used to notify patent owner of proper manner of making amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner of making amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments in an inter partes reexamination proceeding are made in the same manner that amendments in an ex parte reexamination proceeding are made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2250 for guidance as to the manner of making amendments. Form paragraph 22.12 may be used to advise the patent owner of the proper manner of making amendments; form paragraph 26.05.01 may be used to notify patent owner that a proposed amendment does not comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amendment to the specification and/or claims in reexamination must comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), be formally presented pursuant to 37 CFR 1.52(a) and (b), and contain any fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment does not comply, a supplemental paper correctly proposing amendments is required. A shortened statutory period for response (ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer) will be set; failure to timely correct will result in the amendment being held not appropriate and consequences under 37 CFR 1.957(b) or (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing changes — submission format
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner. Upon approval, only new sheets of drawings including the changes and in compliance with § 1.84 must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended,' any added figure as 'New,' and canceled figures surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.' Changes may not be made on original patent drawings. Sketches should be in permanent ink, labeled 'Annotated Sheet,' and become part of the record. If a new sheet contains multiple figures, each figure must be individually marked 'Amended' or 'New' as applicable (header-only marking is insufficient).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of patent drawing copy for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The copy of the patent drawings submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.915(b)(5) will be used for reexamination purposes, provided no change is made to the drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any change is made, a new sheet of drawing for each sheet changed must be submitted; changed sheets should be entered in the reexamination file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship in an inter partes reexamination proceeding is effected in the same manner that correction of inventorship in an ex parte reexamination proceeding is effected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §2250.02 for the manner of correcting inventorship in both inter partes and ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess claims fees applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees specified in 37 CFR 1.20(c) (implementing 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(2)) apply to excess claims proposed to be added to a patent during a reexamination proceeding: the independent-claims fee applies for each independent claim in excess of three and in excess of the number of independent claims in the patent under reexamination; the total-claims fee applies for each claim in excess of twenty and in excess of the number of claims in the patent under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees differ by entity status (micro/small/other). Fees are due only for 'new' (excess) claims resulting from the amendment; revising existing claims without adding new claims does not incur a fee. A claim disclaimed under 35 U.S.C. 253 or canceled in a previous certificate is not considered for fee calculation. If excess claims fees are not paid with the presentation, a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL‑2069) will be issued with a one‑month time for correction; failure to pay may result in termination (37 CFR 1.957(b)) or limitation (37 CFR 1.957(c)). Examples in the text illustrate calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and right to file third-party comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Each time the patent owner files a response to an Office action on the merits pursuant to § 1.945, a third party requester may once file written comments within a period of 30 days from the date of service of the patent owner’s response. These comments shall be limited to issues raised by the Office action or the patent owner’s response. The time for submitting comments by the third party requester may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing date is the date of deposit per the certificate under §1.8. Certificates of mailing/transmission and Priority Mail Express may be used. Comments must be served on the patent owner per 37 CFR 1.248. Late comments (after 30 days) will not be considered (37 CFR 1.957(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on submission of prior art by third party requester
rubrics_metrics.description: After the inter partes reexamination order, the third party requester may only cite additional prior art if filed as part of comments under §1.947 or §1.951(b) and limited to prior art that: (1) is necessary to rebut a finding of fact by the examiner; (2) is necessary to rebut a response of the patent owner; or (3) for the first time became known or available to the third party requester after filing the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art under (3) must be accompanied by a statement explaining when it first became known/available and a discussion of pertinency to at least one claim. Submission of new art does not, by itself, permit a newly proposed rejection unless the patent owner has presented an amendment or new claims that necessitate the rejection. New proposed rejections based on newly presented art must comply with MPEP §2617 and the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 311 (pertinency and explanation of how the art is applied). Substituting new art to replace art originally advanced (i.e., changing the theory for unamended claims) is not permitted as a rebuttal of an examiner finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and form requirements for third-party comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Third party requester comments must be directed to points and issues covered by the Office action and/or the patent owner’s response. The written comments should specify the issue, state the page of the Office action and/or patent owner response where the issue is recited, and then present the requester’s discussion and argument as to the point or issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the requester does not follow this format, the comments should not be held defective if the examiner can ascertain that the comments are directed to issues in the Office action or patent owner response. Comments are limited to issues covered by the Office action or owner response; new prior art is only permitted under the limited circumstances in 37 CFR 1.948(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of improper third-party comments
rubrics_metrics.description: If third party comments are directed to matters other than issues covered by the Office action/patent owner response, or if prior art submitted does not satisfy 1.948(a)(1)-(3), the written comments are improper and should be returned with an explanation; if scanned into IFW they should be expunged with notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If improper comments were filed prior to an Action Closing Prosecution, the requester may be given 15 days to rectify and refile. On second improper submission, comments will be returned and cannot be resubmitted; loss of right to submit further comments applies only to that particular patent owner response. Replacement comments must be strictly limited to the content of the original returned submission (no additions). The provision that requester 'may once' file comments is waived to allow one additional corrective opportunity in these circumstances (but not more). Late or otherwise inappropriate comments are refused without a 15‑day remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on supplemental submissions by requester
rubrics_metrics.description: The third party requester is not permitted to file further papers to supplement the third party requester’s written comments; any such supplemental comments will not be considered and will be returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a third party requester may file written comments to any supplemental response filed by the patent owner. See MPEP §2666.20 for when a requester elects not to file comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on comments when patent owner does not respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent owner does not respond to an Office action, the third party requester is prohibited from filing written comments under 37 CFR 1.947.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third party commenter rights attach only when the patent owner files a response to an Office action on the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art citations submitted as separate papers
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art citation proper under 37 CFR 1.501 that is submitted as a separate paper and does not include argument or go to the merits will not be returned, but will be stored until the reexamination proceeding is concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior art returned by the examiner in connection with third party comments can be resubmitted as a separate prior art citation under 37 CFR 1.501 and will be stored until the proceeding concludes. Such separate prior art submissions do not count as comments under 1.947 and are handled administratively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner withdraws a ground of rejection — treatment and requester options
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner withdraws a ground of rejection at any time, specific guidelines apply depending on whether the rejection was examiner-initiated or originally proposed by the third party requester, and depending on whether claims have been amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) Withdrawal of an examiner-initiated rejection should be stated as a decision favorable to patentability; the requester may propose the withdrawn rejection as a 'rejection proposed by the third party requester' in its next comments and may appeal the withdrawal as a final decision favorable to patentability if a Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) is later issued. (B) If the examiner withdraws a rejection previously proposed by the requester as to unamended claims, treat the issue as a rejection proposed by the requester that the examiner refuses to adopt. (C) If claims have been amended, withdrawal of a previously proposed requester rejection is generally not treated as a refusal to adopt (since the rejection was not proposed as to amended claims), but the requester may propose the rejection anew as to the amended claims. (D) If a claim is amended merely to include a dependent claim previously subjected to a requester rejection and the examiner withdraws the ground, that is a refusal to adopt the requester’s previously proposed rejection of the dependent claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing a request for inter partes reexamination, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on every other party in the reexamination proceeding in the manner provided in 37 CFR 1.248. Any document must reflect service or it may be refused consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As proof of service, attach a certificate of service to the paper setting forth the name and address of the party served and the method of service; a copy of the certificate must be attached to the copy served on the other party. Use PTOL‑2071 as the cover sheet for mailing notices. Failure to serve may result in refusal of consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of service — notice and time to correct
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission appears not to have been served as required, use form paragraph 26.68 to notify the submitting party that the submission is defective for lack of service and require service and a certificate of service within ONE MONTH from the date of the letter or within the time remaining in the response period, whichever is longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 26.68 should be used where a submission to the Office was not served as required in an inter partes reexamination proceeding. See MPEP §2620 for service of the initial request on the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deeming of actual receipt when mailed late
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner’s response that was served on a third party requester is actually received more than 5 business days after the date of service set forth on the certificate of service, the third party requester may submit a verified statement specifying the date of actual receipt; the date of service will then be deemed by the Office to be the date of actual receipt by the third party requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits adjusting the effective service date for purposes of calculating the requester’s 30‑day comment period when mail/service delay occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for unpaid excess claims fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If the excess claims fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) are not paid with the presentation of the excess claims, a Notice of Defective Paper (PTOL‑2069) will be issued setting a one‑month time period to correct the defect; an extension may be requested under 37 CFR 1.956. If unpaid within the time period, the prosecution of the reexamination proceeding will be terminated under 37 CFR 1.957(b) or limited under 37 CFR 1.957(c), as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL‑2069 is the form used for fee deficiency notices. Failure to pay may result in cancellation of claims or other adverse consequences; timely payment avoids abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrow claim construction after patent expiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the patent expires, a narrow claim construction is applied (see MPEP §2258, subsection I.G. 'Claim Interpretation and Treatment').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a substantive assertion about claim interpretation post‑expiration; examiners and practitioners should consult MPEP §2258.I.G for details on how claim interpretation/treatment differs when a patent has expired.
